# Notes

**RMSE:**

- is the difference between the predicted values of the model and the actual observed values

- it is in the same units as the predicted values (unlike RSE, which is unitless)

**Regression for:**

+------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+
| PPA                                                        | Stats                                   |
+============================================================+=========================================+
| For prediction for the future                              | To test robustness of the model         |
|                                                            |                                         |
| - that's why need the CV (Cross-validation)                | - for e.g. inference/hypothesis testing |
|                                                            |                                         |
| - to see how well the dataset performs against unseen data |                                         |
+------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### What is kfolds?

All data gets the opportunity to be the testing dataset.

e.g. if kfolds = 5 ,

1.  data sets split in 5 folds (aka 5 segments)
2.  each segments takes a turn being the test dataset (and the rest of the 4 segments become the training dataset) –\> each turn generates a unique equation + RMSE
3.  the final RMSE is the averaged RMSE of all
4.  the final equation is the equation for 100% of the dataset (no test segment)

- it is done just to see how well the ML model does on untrained data!
